newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes down, on hold before US data.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes down, on hold before US data.

text.p: German shares closed bourse trade lower on Thursday after Wall Street's overnight losses and as German debt fell in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries.

News of a rise in German jobless to record levels and continued modest economic growth prompted some commentators to renew hopes of a cut in German interest rates, but the impact was not enough to have a meaningful effect on shares.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares closed 13.71 points to 2,892.63. March DAX futures traded 8.5 points down at 2,910.0, compared to a morning-low of 2,898.0.

Dealers said there had been some caution in the market before the German data but that investors were really focussing their attention on U.S. producer prices due this afternoon as a clear indication of the extent of U.S. inflationary pressures.
"There are quite a few nerves and volatility out there," one dealer said.
The dollar, trading strongly at 1.577 marks, meanwhile leant some support to share values.

Banks again were among the most active stocks, confirming dealer comments made on Wednesday that investors appeared to be switching out of chemical shares, last year's favourites, into the financial sector.

Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest, closed 85 pfennigs to 74.80 in early dealings while Commerzbank, although slightly weaker at 42.45, managed to hold onto to most of the large gains made it had made on Wednesday.
Car-maker Volkswagen was 15 marks up at 690.50, largely because of the stronger dollar.
Engineering group Siemens turned positive, up 39 pfennigs to 76.79, as sources said it was looking to combine its fossil-fuel power generation operations with those of U.S.-based Westinghouse.
